Figure Reference: Footnotes & Design Notes (ASCE 7-22 Section 30.11, Figures 30.11-1A and 30.11-1B):
[1] Design Wind Pressure Equation (Eq. 30.11-1): p = qh * Kd * (GCp) (psf), where qh is evaluated at mean roof height h of the main building and Kd = 0.85.
[2] Applicability: Attached canopies on walls of buildings with mean roof height h <= 60 ft (18.3 m), canopy height hc < 0.90*he, and canopy maximum slope theta <= 10 degrees.
[3] Notation: hc = height of canopy above ground; he = eaves height of the building (or mean roof height h if flat roof); A = effective wind area (sq ft).
[4] Figure 30.11-1A applies to separate upper or lower surface sheathing/fasteners (e.g., top decking vs. bottom soffit panels).
[5] Figure 30.11-1B applies to combined net pressures acting across both upper and lower surfaces for structural canopy framing, outlooker beams, brackets, tie-back rods, and wall ledger connections.
[6] Linear interpolation is permitted for intermediate values of hc/he.
